theater: 巴比倫尼亞平原、底格里斯河畔

battle.name: 庫麥戰役
battle.theater: 巴比倫尼亞平原、底格里斯河畔
battle.brief: 公元前 401 年 9 月，小居魯士在底格里斯河畔的庫麥挑戰大王阿達薛西二世，一萬三千名希臘傭兵重裝步兵列方陣居中，擋住波斯正面，卻被梯塞斐尼的騎兵迂迴側背。卡面希臘重步兵的方陣正面厚實，仍敵不過阿契美尼德王朝以人數與騎兵取勝的公式。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這是阿契美尼德王朝的一次內戰，交戰雙方同屬波斯帝國，戰場在美索不達米亞下游。大王一方由阿達薛西二世坐鎮御營，營周是近衛「一萬不死軍」與大王騎兵，命令自御營逐級下到行省部隊：呂底亞、卡里亞由梯塞斐尼出軍，亞美尼亞、卡帕多細亞、敘利亞與埃及的步兵騎兵分批北上，呂底亞與亞美尼亞的鎧甲騎兵及數百輛鐮刀車集中在兩翼；梯塞斐尼身兼總督與首席謀臣，實際調度全軍，阿里阿俄斯等波斯貴族分任一翼主將。反叛一方以小居魯士為最高統帥，骨幹是希臘傭兵：克萊亞庫斯率領約六千名重裝步兵，色雷斯人奧龍特斯率領數百名輕裝兵，另有其他希臘步兵，全軍希臘人合計約一萬三千；其餘是波斯與阿美尼亞步兵、弓兵和帕夫拉戈尼亞輕騎。僱傭兵的指揮體系與波斯編制不同：沒有行省與軍團的等級，靠資深軍官組成的將軍會議協商，傭兵領工資、指望戰利品分配，所以小居魯士必須親自在軍中維持士氣。兩軍的戰力結構也不對稱：波斯方靠人數與騎兵迂迴，希臘方靠方陣的正面厚度。
countriesEn: This was a civil war inside the Achaemenid Empire: both sides belonged to the same empire, and the fighting took place in the lower Mesopotamian plain. The Great King's side was commanded from the royal camp by Artaxerxes II, ringed by the guard of the Ten Thousand Immortals and by the King's cavalry, with orders passing down from the camp to the satrapal contingents: Lydians and Carians marched under Tissaphernes, while infantry and horse from Armenia, Cappadocia, Syria and Egypt moved north in separate columns, the armoured cavalry of Lydia and Armenia and some hundreds of scythed chariots being massed on the wings. Tissaphernes was at once satrap and chief counsellor and in practice directed the whole army, while Persian nobles such as Ariaeus commanded wings. The rebel side had Cyrus the Younger as its supreme commander, and its backbone was Greek mercenary infantry: Clearchus led about six thousand hoplites, Orontes the Thracian led some hundreds of peltasts, other Greek foot were present, and the Greek contingent in the army totalled about thirteen thousand; the rest was Persian and Armenian infantry, archers and Paphlagonian light horse. The mercenary command system was not the satrapal and corps structure of the Persian army: with no grades and no regiments, it worked through a council of senior officers, the mercenaries drawing their pay and counting on a share of the plunder, so Cyrus had to keep their spirits up in person. The two armies were also asymmetrical in shape: the Persian side relied on numbers and on cavalry envelopment, the Greek side on the thickness of the phalanx in front.
people: 小居魯士是此役的另一主角。他是大流士一世與其妻帕里薩所生的次子，與長兄阿達薛西爭位；公元前 407 年他與底比斯聯軍在敘利亞境內的幼發拉底河擊敗大王的一支軍隊，卻無法把王位拿到手，於是改用另一條路：在薩迪斯與小亞細亞西岸招募傭兵，用金錢和「戰利品共享」的承諾把一批希臘人買到旗下，據說還在軍中散播大王名分不正、他更有資格繼承的說法。阿達薛西二世在會戰中坐鎮御營，他的坐騎在混亂中受驚，衛兵以盾結成人牆才護得他脫身。梯塞斐尼是全軍最具攻擊性的指揮者，他統率一翼，看準希臘方陣的側翼，率騎兵迂迴其背後，會戰後主持追擊，往後數年又以金錢、爵位與土地招撫希臘將領。阿里阿俄斯統率另一翼，擊潰反叛軍的左翼後率騎兵追擊撤退的方陣，日後因不滿阿達薛西而起兵反叛，反被梯塞斐尼平定。希臘方面的核心是克萊亞庫斯，這位出身斯巴達的將領以嚴厲聞名，他率重裝步兵列於全軍中央，會戰中頂住波斯正面，退卻時仍以方陣保持完整；色雷斯人奧龍特斯率領的輕裝兵在撤退途中倒戈投向波斯。色諾芬是隨軍見證者，把會戰與隨後的退路寫成《回程記》第一卷，成為此役最可靠的文字記錄。
peopleEn: The other protagonist of the battle was Cyrus the Younger, second son of Darius I and Queen Parisa, in dispute with his elder brother Artaxerxes. In 407 BC he and the Thebans defeated a royal army at the Euphrates in Syria but could not take the throne, so he took another road: he hired mercenaries at Sardis and on the western coast of Asia Minor, buying a body of Greeks with money and with the promise of shared plunder, and he is said to have spread among them the claim that the Great King had no right to the throne and that he was the better heir. Artaxerxes II sat in the royal camp during the fight, his horse was startled in the confusion, and only a wall of shields formed by his guard carried him clear. Tissaphernes was the most aggressive commander in the army: he led a wing, marked the flank of the Greek phalanx, rode round behind it with the cavalry, took over the pursuit afterwards, and in later years bought off Greek officers with money, rank and land. Ariaeus commanded the other wing, destroyed the rebel left and then pursued the retreating square with his horse; he later rose in revolt against Artaxerxes and was put down by Tissaphernes. At the heart of the Greek side was Clearchus, a Spartan by birth and famous for his severity, who led the hoplites in the centre of the line, held the Persian front, and kept the phalanx intact even while withdrawing; the peltasts of Orontes the Thracian went over to the Persians during the retreat. Xenophon was present as a witness and set down the battle and the road back in the first book of the Anabasis, which remains the most reliable written record of the affair.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵，配備是典型的五世紀式樣：頭戴青銅科林式頭盔，前有長而窄的鼻梁飾與可翻起的護頰，頸甲保護後腦與頸部；上身是青銅或亞麻製的胸甲，扣在肩帶與腰帶之間，兩側加護胯，下著青銅脛甲；左手持直徑約九十厘米的圓盾，盾面常以青銅貼片加強，盾緣相扣即可連成一道牆；右手持約二米長的單柄長矛，矛尖是鐵製的菱形矛頭，杆後留有反手用的鐵鉤，盾扣上還插著一柄約六十厘米的葉形短劍。整套裝備連同武器約二十至二十五公斤，因此重裝步兵只能以步行方陣作戰。庫麥的會戰裡，這支部隊約六千人列在反叛全軍正中：正面頂住波斯步兵與弓手的推壓，兩翼由波斯與阿美尼亞步兵、帕夫拉戈尼亞騎兵掩護。它在戰場上展現出方陣的優點，前排矛尖在盾後構成刺面，縱深八排、層層舉矛，個人動作讓位於整體；同一刻也暴露弱點，一旦側背被騎兵切斷，隊形必須停下轉為四面作戰，包圍而來的騎兵可以從任何方向撕開前排。波斯方的主要裝備是短弓與標槍，配圓盾或方盾、束腰長袍與魚鱗式鐵片甲，兩翼集中大量鎧甲騎兵與鐮刀車；鐮刀車在陣前列陣，運載貴族與傳令，未曾投入衝鋒。希臘方另有帳幕、軍需車隊與載人車行軍，僱傭兵的補給靠工資與戰利品維持，波斯方則以行省徵發的糧秣供給遠在薩迪斯的御營。
kitsEn: The hoplite on the card is equipped in the classic fifth-century fashion: a bronze Corinthian helmet with a long narrow nose-piece and a hinged cheek-piece, its neck guard covering the back of the head and neck; a bronze or linen corselet clasped between shoulder and waist belts, with side plates over the hips; bronze greaves on the shins; in the left hand a round shield about ninety centimetres across, its face often strengthened with bronze patches, and the rims overlapping so that they could be locked into a wall; in the right hand a single-piece spear about two metres long with an iron leaf-shaped head and a rear spike for pulling it back, and a leaf-shaped short sword of about sixty centimetres hanging in the shield strap. The whole load with weapons came to roughly twenty to twenty-five kilograms, which is why hoplites fought on foot in phalanx. At Cunaxa about six thousand of them stood in the centre of the rebel army: they held the Persian front against the pushing of foot and bow, with Persian and Armenian infantry and Paphlagonian horse covering their flanks. On the field they showed what the phalanx could do, the front rank's spear points forming a hedge of points behind the shields, eight files deep with each rank's spears raised over the shoulders of the one in front, the individual giving way to the whole; at the same moment they showed its weakness, for once the flank and rear were cut the line had to halt and turn to fight in every direction, and the cavalry that closed in could open the front from any side. The Persian equipment was the short bow and the javelin, with round or square shields, belted tunics and scale-like iron plating, and the wings held masses of armoured cavalry and scythed chariots; the chariots were deployed in front of the line, to carry nobles and messengers, and were never driven into the charge. The Greeks also had tents, baggage trains and carriers for their marching, and the mercenaries lived on their pay and their plunder, while the Persian host was fed by the levies of the satrapies all the way back to Sardis.
tactics: 波斯方的戰術公式很清楚：以全軍人數壓上，用兩翼騎兵做迂迴，不在正面硬碰。開戰之後，希臘重裝步兵主動出擊，擊退波斯前線，陣線一度推進；與此同時梯塞斐尼所率的一翼大敗反叛軍的左翼，隨即勒轉兵鋒，帶著大批騎兵繞到希臘方陣的側背，把正面消耗變成三面受敵。希臘方陣被迫收緊，改成四面都能作戰的密集隊形，前排的盾互相抵住撐住，槍尖朝外，隊形內的人被自己的重裝備釘在原地，動作只限於刺擊。梯塞斐尼的騎兵沒有正面硬衝，而在外圍以弓箭與標槍削弱方陣的邊緣，等人數與縱深被吃掉一部分再整批衝入。就在此時，小居魯士帶著數百名精兵直撲梯塞斐尼那一部，企圖把那支迂迴部隊切斷，兩軍在方陣側後混成一團，小居魯士在亂軍中直衝阿達薛西，坐騎被標槍擊中，他在落馬時陣亡。希臘方陣在損失慘重之後開始撤退，退路本身就是戰術：全軍收成一個中空的方陣，四面盾牌朝外，排成一團緩慢行進，波斯騎兵在其周圍反覆衝擊而難以下手；入夜之後暴雨落下，追兵失去追擊的能力，次日清早方陣仍保持原狀行軍，並在底格里斯河一處水勢平緩處渡河。希臘方的方陣與波斯方的騎兵迂迴，正好是卡面那句話的兩面：盾牌接在一起時正面比個人結實，但方陣的前提是正面完整。
tacticsEn: The Persian formula was plain: press with the whole army, envelop with the cavalry on the wings, and do not try to win in the front. When the battle opened the Greek hoplites attacked of their own accord, drove back the Persian front, and at one point carried the line forward; at the same time the wing under Tissaphernes broke the rebel left, wheeled, and rode round to the flank and rear of the Greek square, turning frontal pressure into attack on three sides. The phalanx tightened into a formation that could fight in every direction, the shields of the front rank braced against one another, the spear points facing out, the men pinned in place by their own weight and equipment, their movement reduced to the thrust. Tissaphernes' cavalry did not charge the front but worked round it, weakening the edges of the square with arrows and javelins, and then came in in mass once numbers and depth had been eaten away. It was then that Cyrus led several hundred picked men straight at Tissaphernes' part of the line, trying to cut off the enveloping force; the two armies tangled behind the square, Cyrus charged Artaxerxes, his horse was struck by a javelin, and he fell and died. The Greek phalanx, badly hit, began to withdraw, and the withdrawal was itself a tactic: the whole force closed into a hollow square, shields outward on all four sides, moving slowly as a mass, with the Persian horse charging round it again and again and finding no purchase. A violent storm came down in the night, the pursuit lost its chance, and in the morning the square was still in order on the march and crossed the Tigris at a stretch where the water ran slack. The Greek phalanx and the Persian cavalry envelopment are the two faces of the line on the card: when the shields are locked together the front is stronger than a single man, but the phalanx presupposes an intact front.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且多帶誇張。色諾芬記小居魯士軍中的希臘傭兵約一萬三千人，其中克萊亞庫斯的重裝步兵約六千，色雷斯人奧龍特斯部的輕裝兵數百，此外還有波斯與阿美尼亞步兵、弓兵和帕夫拉戈尼亞騎兵，全軍總數古代記述多估在二萬至三萬之間；波斯大軍的總數沒有可靠記載，說法從數萬到逾十萬不等，現代學者多視為誇大，但無疑遠多於反叛軍。戰場在巴比倫以北約六十至七十公里、底格里斯河左岸的平原，希臘方面自戰場退到河岸約二十餘公里。傷亡方面，色諾芬記會戰當日希臘方面陣亡約二百人，撤退途中再折損約七百人，被俘者約一千四百人；波斯方面的損失集中在被正面擊退的那一翼，沒有可靠數字。會戰時間在夏末秋初，傳統定於公元前 401 年 9 月初，此役也常被列為希臘與波斯戰爭的最後一場會戰。年份上有一處需要說明：戰爭列表把此條記在公元前 474 年，而古代記錄與後世研究一致把它定在公元前 401 年，本卡沿用列表編號，敘事以史料年代為準。裝備重量方面，重裝步兵全套連武器約二十至二十五公斤，長矛約二米，圓盾直徑約九十厘米；波斯大軍的御營仍在薩迪斯方向，糧秣線橫穿幼發拉底河，長達數百公里，靠各行省徵發維持。
dataEn: There are not many figures that can be checked, and most of them are inflated. Xenophon gives about thirteen thousand Greek mercenaries in Cyrus' army, of whom about six thousand were Clearchus' hoplites and some hundreds peltasts under Orontes the Thracian, alongside Persian and Armenian infantry, archers and Paphlagonian horse, and ancient accounts put the whole force anywhere between twenty and thirty thousand; there is no reliable figure for the Persian host, estimates running from tens of thousands to over a hundred thousand, which modern scholars generally treat as exaggeration, though the Persian side was plainly much the larger. The field of battle lay on the left bank of the Tigris, some sixty to seventy kilometres north of Babylon, and the Greeks covered roughly twenty kilometres or more from the field to the river. For losses, Xenophon records about two hundred of the Greeks killed on the day of the battle, several hundred more lost in the retreat, and about fourteen hundred taken prisoner; the Persian losses fell on the wing that was driven back in the front and no figure survives. The battle was fought in the late summer and early autumn, traditionally early September 401 BC, and the affair is often listed as the last pitched battle of the Greek wars against Persia. There is one point about the dating to be noted: the list of wars enters this item under 474 BC, whereas the ancient sources and later scholarship alike put it in 401 BC; the card keeps the number of the list, and the narrative follows the dating of the sources. On weights, a hoplite carried twenty to twenty-five kilograms with his weapons, his spear was about two metres long and his round shield about ninety centimetres across. The royal camp of the Persian army still lay back towards Sardis, and its line of supply crossed the Euphrates over a distance of several hundred kilometres, maintained by the levies of the satrapies.
cause: 起因是阿契美尼德王朝的繼承危機。大流士一世去世後，王位由長子阿達薛西二世繼承，弟弟小居魯士不服；生母帕里薩站在小居魯士一邊，呂底亞、卡里亞與敘利亞的部分行省貴族也倒向他，公元前 407 年他聯同底比斯在幼發拉底河擊敗大王的一支軍隊，卻沒有能力把王位奪到手。公元前 406 年冬，小居魯士作出決定：不再等援軍，先發制人。他帶著希臘傭兵自薩迪斯出發，沿小亞細亞東行，渡過幼發拉底河，進入大王的心臟地帶巴比倫尼亞，企圖在御營奪位。希臘傭兵是他手中最鋒利的武器：他用金錢招募，用「戰利品由參戰者共享」的承諾留住人，據說在軍中散播大王不配上王位、而他更有資格繼承的說法；對這些靠契約與戰利品維生的軍人而言，替王子作戰是一樁有收益的買賣。對阿達薛西而言，這是必須消滅的叛亂：只要小居魯士一天帶著軍隊在，希臘人一天就會看到帝國王權的裂縫，而大王在薩迪斯的宮廷正被這種裂縫威脅。從希臘世界的角度，庫麥其實是希臘與波斯三十年戰爭的收尾：這是一場以希臘傭兵為主力、由波斯內部派系打起來的戰爭，希臘人從中第一次近距離看見王位之爭，也第一次拿自己的方陣去撞阿契美尼德的騎兵。
causeEn: The cause was a crisis of succession in the Achaemenid house. After the death of Darius I the throne passed to his elder son Artaxerxes II, and the younger brother Cyrus refused to accept it; the queen-mother Parisa stood with Cyrus, and the nobility of Lydia, Caria and parts of Syria went over to him. In 407 BC Cyrus and the Thebans beat a royal army at the Euphrates, but he could not take the throne, so in the winter of 406 BC he decided to strike first. He marched out of Sardis with his Greek mercenaries, moved east through Asia Minor, crossed the Euphrates and entered Babylonia, the heart of the King's dominions, in the hope of taking the camp itself. The Greek mercenaries were the sharpest instrument he had: he hired them with money and kept them with the promise that plunder would be shared among those who fought, and the story goes that he spread among them the claim that the Great King did not deserve the throne. For Artaxerxes this was a rebellion that had to be destroyed: as long as Cyrus was alive with an army, the Greeks would go on seeing the crack in the imperial power, and the court at Sardis was itself threatened by that crack. From the Greek point of view, Cunaxa was the closing piece of thirty years of war between Greece and Persia: a war fought with Greek mercenary infantry as its main force, started by the rival factions of Persia, in which the Greeks saw the struggle for the throne at close quarters and put their own phalanx up against the cavalry of the Achaemenids for the first time.
impact: 對波斯帝國，這一場內戰把王位繼承的危機一次性解決：阿達薛西坐穩王位，小居魯士一系的軍事資源被清剿。帝國此後把注意力轉向埃及與亞洲腹地，與希臘的直接衝突退居次要，而希臘傭兵在波斯內戰中的角色反而越來越重，四百年後亞歷山大大帝東征時，希臘方陣的後裔已大量編入波斯與希臘聯軍，庫麥的經驗就成了他們的教科書。對希臘世界，這一戰留下的是一套用文字固化的記憶：色諾芬的《回程記》第一卷記錄會戰與撤退，是古典時期最著名的軍事冒險文學，歐里庇得斯的悲劇《波斯人》把「波斯內戰、希臘人為工具」寫成悲劇母題，後世講究兵法與將略的人反覆從中提煉方陣的用法與騎兵迂迴的危險。戰術層面的教訓最實際：希臘重裝步兵的方陣能在正面吃掉波斯步兵與弓兵，卻無法抵擋不受地形限制的騎兵迂迴；一旦方陣被切成三面，縱深再厚也只能變成一個被困住的目標。這條教訓在希臘兵的僱傭生涯裡被反覆重演，之後數百年的希臘化東方僱傭軍都靠分遣小方陣與騎兵遮護來避免同樣的結局。經濟上，希臘傭兵的市場被這次內戰推高，呂底亞與卡里亞的財富被大量運作軍費，希臘城邦的年輕人成批流向亞洲。庫麥之後，雙方的和解並不徹底：小居魯士留下的部將阿里阿俄斯與希臘將領克萊亞庫斯，都在往後數年裡以背叛收場，讓這場戰役在希臘人口述中成為一則關於僱傭兵忠誠的教訓。
impactEn: For the Persian empire the civil war settled the succession question in a single stroke: Artaxerxes sat secure on the throne and the military resources of Cyrus' party were liquidated. The empire turned its attention to Egypt and the interior of Asia, and open collision with Greece became a secondary matter, while the role of Greek mercenaries in Persian internal wars grew steadily; four centuries later, when Alexander marched east, the descendants of the phalanx were already enrolled in large numbers in both Persian and Greek armies, and the lesson of Cunaxa was their textbook. For the Greek world the battle left behind a memory fixed in writing: the first book of Xenophon's Anabasis records the battle and the retreat in what is the most famous piece of military adventure literature of the classical age, and Euripides' tragedy The Persians turned the theme of a Persian civil war in which the Greeks are the instruments into a tragic subject, from which men of the art of war have drawn again and again both the use of the phalanx and the danger of cavalry envelopment. The tactical lesson was the most practical of all: the Greek phalanx could consume the Persian foot and bowmen in front, but it could not withstand cavalry envelopment unconstrained by terrain; once the square was attacked on three sides, however deep it was, it became only a trapped target. That lesson was repeated through the whole mercenary career of the Greek soldiers, and the eastern Greek hireling armies of the centuries that followed all tried to avoid the same end by detaching small squares and screening them with horse. Economically the war inflated the market for Greek mercenaries, the wealth of Lydia and Caria was spent on wages, and the young men of the Greek cities streamed towards Asia. The reconciliation after Cunaxa was never complete: Ariaeus, one of Cyrus' officers, and the Greek commander Clearchus both met their ends in treachery within a few years, and the battle entered Greek oral tradition as a lesson in the loyalty of mercenaries.
result: 結果是波斯勝、小居魯士死、希臘方陣幾乎全身而退。大王軍在會戰中以梯塞斐尼所率的一翼擊潰反叛軍左翼，迂迴包抄希臘方陣的側背；小居魯士率精兵反衝迂迴部隊時陣亡，阿達薛西的御營保住了。希臘方面雖然被切斷，卻沒有被摧毀：克萊亞庫斯的方陣在混戰中仍保持緊密，退卻時以中空方陣行軍，最後渡過底格里斯河，這支部隊回到小亞細亞西岸的同盟城市重整，後來成為《回程記》所說的「萬人軍」，在沒有後方的情況下穿越亞美尼亞與高加索，再沿海路回到黑海。會戰之後，阿達薛西下令搜尋小居魯士的遺體，希臘人在其營帳中交出；梯塞斐尼接管巴比倫尼亞的軍權，並以金錢、爵位與土地招撫希臘將領，這種手段在數年之後屢次得手。戰敗的希臘人也在自己的營地裡分裂：色雷斯人奧龍特斯與部眾在撤退途中投奔波斯，阿里阿俄斯集兵於小亞細亞後又舉兵反叛大王，被梯塞斐尼擊敗；克萊亞庫斯等將領則在往後數年被梯塞斐尼以宴會與毒殺除掉。於是庫麥的真正結局不是雙方的全滅，而是各有所得：波斯保住了王朝，卻放走一批能打的希臘方陣；希臘人帶走了一套完整的軍事學問，卻沒有帶走任何波斯土地。
resultEn: The result was a Persian victory, the death of Cyrus the Younger and the near-total escape of the Greek phalanx. The King's army broke the rebel left with the wing under Tissaphernes, enveloped the flank and rear of the Greek square, and when Cyrus charged back at the enveloping force with his picked men he was killed and the royal camp stood. The Greek force was cut off but not destroyed: Clearchus' phalanx stayed compact through the melee, marched away in a hollow square, and crossed the Tigris, reaching the allied cities of western Asia Minor to be reformed, and it became the force the Anabasis calls the Ten Thousand, crossing Armenia and the Caucasus with no base behind it and coming back to the Black Sea along the coast. After the battle Artaxerxes ordered a search for Cyrus' body, which the Greeks handed over from his camp; Tissaphernes took over the military command in Babylonia and drew Greek officers in with money, rank and land, a method that succeeded repeatedly in the years that followed. The defeated Greeks also split among themselves: Orontes the Thracian and his men went over to the Persians on the march, Ariaeus mustered troops in Asia Minor after the retreat and rebelled against the Great King, and was defeated by Tissaphernes, while Clearchus and the other officers were removed by Tissaphernes' banquet and poison within a few years. The real ending of Cunaxa was therefore not mutual destruction but a divided prize: Persia saved its dynasty but let go a body of Greek hoplites who could fight; the Greeks carried away a complete set of military lessons but brought no Persian territory with them.
